💡 Key Takeaways
  • Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums.
  • Industry observers note that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics.
  • Apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple owners saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a new laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

Industry observers note that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you strategy to buy a newly introduced laptop while there are holiday savings.

Apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple owners saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

Sources indicate that apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

How much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple users paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” said Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

In a recent development, if you blueprint to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — right now MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

Recent findings suggest that apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple users mentioned their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

Industry observers note that digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple people seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

Take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple users may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

Battery life is a substantial deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) said their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook customers saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

Comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo users say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test shows that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

Apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its customers either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

“Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” said Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

Sources indicate that the upcoming MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook users have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.

Industry observers note that and MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple consumers reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their challenges. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.

Sources indicate that our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.

“Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” noted Goldman.

Lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it states encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.

Sources indicate that when it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple consumers reported poor performance.

Here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without challenges or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.

On the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple consumers rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.

Apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple users planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.

In a recent development, usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.

Asus wins as a midtier laptop choice with 67% of Asus owners paying between $500 and $1,499. There’s a sweet spot in this range with 38% spending between $500 and $999, and 28% paying between $1,000 and $1,499.

If you’re planning to spend that amount on a fresh laptop, you may also be pleased to know that Asus earns a higher satisfaction rating compared with other non-Apple laptop brands — 48% of Asus customers say they’re extremely satisfied.

It has been revealed that asus laptops have a few features and specifications that may speak to that rating, regardless of budget. For example, the Zenbook A14 has a thin, lightweight design that’s rigid, with long battery life and an OLED display with strong contrast and color performance. This Copilot Plus PC sells for $1,600 (but retailers like Best Buy regularly have it on sale for less). Comparatively, these premium features from other brands could cost more or sacrifice important must-have features for the price.

Asus has other laptops worth exploring depending on your needs, like the budget-friendly Asus ZenBook S 14 or the premium Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 that could be good for gamers and creators.

Over one-third of Acer laptop owners (38%) paid less than $500 for their laptop — which is greater than other laptop brands in this price range. Yet, 44% of Acer users say their laptop has exceptional value, while 50% say the value is fair — bringing a total positive cost-to-value score of over 94%. Acer also has an overall satisfaction score of 92.6% — the highest of non-Apple laptop brands.

If you’re impressed by Acer’s value and satisfaction scores, there are a few budget-friendly Acer options to consider. The Acer Aspire 16 AI wins CNET’s Editors’ Choice award. It has a big 16-inch screen but is still lightweight (3.5 pounds). And it has good battery life (over 21 hours on CNET’s battery drain test). There are a few other pluses, like the 1440p web camera that may be good for video conferencing and a sizable touchpad. All of those features and more add up to $700, which could make it a good computer for work or casual browsing. If you’re looking to spend slightly less, its predecessor, the Aspire 14 AI, is originally $639, but you may be able to score deals on both models during holiday sales.

Even though Apple is highly recommended by CNET readers, there are plenty of other laptop models and brands worth considering depending on your needs. Here are a few non-Apple laptop brands that are runner-ups to CNET’s People’s Picks winners that you shouldn’t count out of your laptop search.

Sources indicate that lenovo is best known for packing a powerful laptop into a compact design with tablet functionality, like its Yoga line, and its durable ThinkPad business models. But CNET readers with Lenovo laptops say the brand’s battery life stands out most compared with other non-MacBook laptops.

According to recent reports, survey findings show that 16% of Lenovo owners say their laptops can run for 8 hours or more. And 10.5% say their laptop battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours, while 6% say their Lenovo laptops can withstand at least 10 hours before needing a charge. That’s more than what readers say about other non-Apple brands. The Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition lasts 25 hours and 45 minutes — making it one of the best laptop batteries CNET experts have tested.

Goldman noted Lenovo has such a large and varied PC selection using the latest chips from Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Nvidia that there is something for everyone and every budget. Even those who spend less on a Lenovo laptop can expect solid performance, including battery life.

It has been revealed that if your laptop’s hardware fails or it breaks, you may be in the market for a newly introduced laptop sooner than expected. Think about cooling fan problems, overheating or your laptop not powering on at all. Over half (68%) of Lenovo laptop owners stated they haven’t had any hardware challenges with their laptops — the most compared to other non-MacBooks.

Recent findings suggest that beyond hardware durability, Lenovo also scores highly for its build and construction — overall making it a sturdy laptop choice. In our survey, 38% of Lenovo laptop owners say their laptop has a premium feel, while 51% say it’s solid — totaling a positive score of 89%.

If you’re looking for recommendations, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 has an all-metal design. And the Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 is a business laptop with Lenovo’s well-known X1 Carbon exterior and upcoming Space Frame design, which Elliott indicates makes it easier to repair or replace parts if needed.

Many Lenovo laptop users are loyal to the brand, which speaks to the overall positive satisfaction rating of 83%. If Lenovo owners were in the market for a upcoming laptop, nearly three in four (73.2%) say they would buy another Lenovo laptop. Breaking down the percentage, 33.6% say they would buy the same model again. Meanwhile, 39.6% would buy a different model but stick to Lenovo.

Here’s why that might be. Lenovo offers a plethora of options to choose from based on your needs — while still evolving its laptops. For instance, the Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 10 has an open M.2 slot for a second storage drive and an OLED screen for crisp, colorful images — making it perfect for gaming. Its Yoga two-in-ones let you seamlessly switch between a tablet and traditional laptop, while Lenovo’s ThinkPad and ThinkBook business laptops offer everything from ultralight 2-pound bodies to expanding rollable screens. And its upcoming designs don’t sacrifice the must-have needs like long battery life, durability and chip efficiency that lend to strong performance.

Asus wins over nearly half of its laptop owners, with 47.5% giving it an exceptional value rating  — exceeding expectations for its price. Take our Editors’ Choice pick, the Asus Zenbook A14. It’s super thin and lightweight, but it’s still sturdy thanks to its Ceralumnium body. Plus, it has supreme 24-hour battery life, 1TB of storage and an OLED display — all for $1,200. While that’s more expensive than some laptops, it’s what’s included in that price that makes it worthwhile compared with other non-Apple laptop brands.

Asus is the top non-Apple laptop option to consider for tasks, with 47.7% of CNET readers giving it high ratings. That’s followed by 40.4% of Asus laptop owners who say it has very good task performance. When it comes to tasks, 37% primarily use their Asus laptops for work, while 5% use theirs for gaming.

In a recent development, asus is well known for having lightweight laptops with all-day-and-night battery life and stunning display quality. Asus laptops like the Asus ROG Zephyrus G16 have a good port selection, which could be good for gaming, work or simply connecting different devices without the need for additional adapters. And the Asus Zenbook S 14 has a strong neural processing unit that contributes to its high-speed AI performance.

Industry observers note that asus scores highest for its screen brightness and clarity, with over half (51%) extremely satisfied with its screen quality and brightness, while 38.6% say they’re satisfied, giving Asus an overall satisfaction rate of 90%. One common thread we noticed in Asus laptops is their OLED screens, which deliver high-resolution video and graphics. Asus laptops also combine stunning display quality with excellent performance and at surprisingly low prices for all of their features.

Recent findings suggest that for example, the Asus Zenbook 14 isn’t the highest-quality OLED we’ve seen, but it still produces clear text and graphics on a 14-inch screen, along with exceptional black levels, Elliott said. That’s still better than LCDs that many other non-MacBooks have, and could be the reason Asus owners rate it so highly in this category.

In a recent development, dell wins our readers over as a top choice for high-end laptops. One-third (33.3%) of Dell owners spent over $1,500, and of that percentage, 15.2% spent over $2,000.

Sources indicate that dell’s premium laptops largely cater to business and gaming with their standout features and performance. The Alienware 16X Aurora is Dell’s midrange gaming laptop with user-replaceable RAM, a bright display and strong performance for $2,280. But if you want more gaming features, Dell has the Alienware 16 Area-51, which has even better gaming performance, upgradable RAM and three SSD slots for $2,530. And if you’re looking for a non-Mac alternative that comes close to MacBook quality and performance, the higher-end Dell XPS 14 is the one to choose. It has the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 graphics and 1TB of storage for $1,950.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption.
  • During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella confirmed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
  • Also: Microsoft says its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella confirmed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several newly introduced Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft noted. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft noted, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s latest Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

Sources indicate that “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft stated.

It has been revealed that the organization added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also unveiled a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. At the moment in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft noted of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

It has been revealed that microsoft also unveiled that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft revealed a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the firm’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft revealed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

According to recent reports, “It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft noted. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

Recent findings suggest that “Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft stated. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise intends.

Industry News: Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
  • It has been revealed that A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov.
  • Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

It has been revealed that A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

Back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

It has been revealed that an Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

It has been revealed that apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and users. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

When news of the shutdown spread, Apple owners flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

Sources indicate that for many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

Recent findings suggest that in discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community users to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others said the site grew less helpful over the years.

It has been revealed that CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he stated.

Industry observers note that just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

The shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push users away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

According to recent reports, reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual customers to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

Apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The organization may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum people on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

Recent findings suggest that whatever the reason, the circle of Apple users helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar plans.

Tech Report: Microsoft’s new Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several latest models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company.
  • Also: Microsoft claims its newly introduced AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • Industry observers note that MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several latest models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft claims its newly introduced AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

Industry observers note that MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, noted during the keynote.

Industry observers note that the approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft mentioned it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman remarked during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

According to recent reports, the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the manufacturer has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Sources indicate that western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company unveiled at Ignite.

Industry observers note that the company also released its upcoming image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip revision, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

It has been revealed that everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

The latest Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:.

Sources indicate that the complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a latest Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

It has been revealed that most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

Industry observers note that more battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:.

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off quickly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

Have you upgraded to Apple Watch Series 12? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

#62442. Inkling 2 Mini

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3148 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thinkingmachines ↗ Open Full Page

Inkling 2 Mini

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3148 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thinkingmachines

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.
  • Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token.
  • Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well.

SWE-bench Pro v2 Hard (51 tasks).

Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping. Looping allows the model to reason longer without writing its reasoning down, which matters for monitoring: our ability to oversee and understand what the model does by reading its chain of thought (CoT).

We measured the impact of looping on both performance and monitorability with Inkling 2 Mini and a research-specific variable-loop variant we are releasing alongside it. The variable-loop model’s no-CoT time horizon improved from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds with three, and its performance on a benchmark of serial reasoning kept improving out to ten loops—twice as many as it was trained with. The model’s chain of thought grew shorter with more loops but stayed legible throughout. The model didn’t trend higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.

We’re excited to offer some of the first models with looped architecture available to researchers. The variable-loop model was used for our monitorability experiments as it allows for cleaner comparisons between different looping depths.

Most of Inkling 2 Mini’s weights were trained and are deployed natively in NVFP4, with the last four layers in MXFP8. The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers. Our researchers took Inkling 2 Mini on a flight, where it ran offline on a MacBook Pro and built a playable flight simulator in a few minutes.

Inkling 2 Mini is released with open weights and is available on Tinker today for inference and customization.

Inkling 2 Mini’s strengths mirror those of Inkling 2 Small: it does best on long-horizon agentic work and is the best among open-weights models of similar size on most tasks we measured.

Inkling 2 Mini scores ahead of every comparable model on agentic coding benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 and SWE-bench Pro v2, and is behind only Qwen3.8-27B on others. On PMPP-Hard, a kernel-optimization benchmark, it approaches the score of the much larger Inkling 2 Small.

While looping improves the model’s reasoning, it doesn’t enable its weights to store more facts—knowledge is mostly a function of total parameter count. Inkling 2 Mini’s score on AA-Omniscience, a measure of factuality, is in line with other models of the same size. Studying the variable-loop model, we saw that performances on long-context benchmarks improve with more passes, such as GraphWalks BFS and MRCR v2; but knowledge-intensive benchmarks doesn’t improve with more passes, such as AA-Omniscience, SimpleQA Verified, SimpleVQA, and WorldVQA.

Inkling 2 Mini overcomes the knowledge gap by efficiently using search and tools. It leads open-weights models of similar size on BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, and MCP Atlas. It is also strong on knowledge work benchmarks that incorporate search and tool use.

According to recent reports, researchers at Stanford measure intelligence per joule: how much energy an LLM needs per query to reach a given level of performance.Researchers at Stanford’s Hazy Research Lab and Scaling Intelligence Lab got early testing access to Inkling 2 Mini. Inkling 2 Mini scored 0.703 running on NVIDIA DGX Spark, significantly higher than other models: 0.430 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 0.159 for Gemma-4-26B-A4B and 0.036 for Qwen3.5-27B.Intelligence per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI, Saad-Falcon and Narayan et al., 2025Inkling 2 Mini ran on NVIDIA DGX Spark (128GB) at MXFP8 precision with low reasoning effort in this experiment. The other models ran at NVFP4 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B) and INT4 (Qwen3.5-27B).

Efficiency combined with performance makes Inkling 2 Mini a strong choice for running multiple persistent agents on local hardware. All 20 residents of the energy-conscious village of Thinkyville are managed by Inkling 2 Mini running on a single offline MacBook.

According to recent reports, inkling 2 Mini is not the strongest small model for multi-turn chat or for instructions with many constraints: it scores 50.0% on MultiChallenge and 33.4% on ComplexConstraints v1.1, behind Qwen3.8-27B on both. It also trails larger models on reasoning-intensive benchmarks such as CritPt v2 and HLE-Diamond.

Sources indicate that inkling 2 Mini is a 24-layer model derived from our mainline predictive scaling ladder. The main changes from the mainline recipe were pruning two-thirds of the experts to reduce the model’s size and the introduction of looping to improve reasoning. The rest of training, including quantization and the data mix, followed our mainline recipe.

According to recent reports, inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, divided into four blocks of six layers each. The two middle blocks run three times, while the first and last blocks each run once. This design builds on prior work on looped transformers and is motivated by the intuition that the middle layers of the model carry more abstract reasoning, while the first and last few layers devote more space to translating between embeddings and internal representations.Universal Transformers, Dehghani et al., 2018 In our experiments, looping the middle 12 layers resulted in larger gains in accuracy than looping the last 12 on 27 out of 28 different evaluations.

Compute-equivalent gain by loop position.

Sources indicate that our model uses attention residuals.Attention Residuals, Kimi Team: Guangyu Chen et al., 2026 Instead of adding every layer’s output into one running sum, each layer reads the outputs of the earlier blocks and learns its own mix of them. This allows richer information to pass between loops. Every pass starts with the output of the prelude (the first block). The second and third passes through the middle blocks also read the middle blocks’ outputs from the previous pass, which we call the message.

Recent findings suggest that the previous loop’s message is merged with the prelude’s output via a gate that scales these along with the output of the previous layers in the block. This gate is learned during training: it initially blocks the entire message—which makes each loop start the same as in a non-looping model—and increases the gain on the message over time. This allows us to introduce looping during training in a stable manner.

Sources indicate that to evaluate the impact of looping, we compared an unpruned looping version to the unpruned non-looping model on our scaling ladder. The non-looping model cost 7.5% less compute to train, but required 140% more inference compute to match the looped version’s loss on 512k-token agentic traces.

It has been revealed that inkling 2 Mini was trained with 4-bit precision, which we describe in a recent article on Connectionism. We use 4-bit NVFP4 precision in the expert layers on all forward passes from pretraining through RL, bolstered by a dedicated kernel and hardware-accelerated on NVIDIA’s GB300 platform. The final 4 layers’ forward passes ran in 8-bit (MXFP8).

Inkling 2 Mini’s weights are deployed in the same numeric precision they were trained on—20 layers in NVFP4 and 4 in MXFP8—so there is no conversion loss from quantization.

Industry observers note that inkling 2 Mini started training with a sparsity of 48, with 8 experts being chosen out of 384. At a single point during midtraining, we pruned two-thirds of the experts, leaving the 128 experts that were most used in each layer. This was done to cut the total parameter count of the model, allowing it to run faster and on local hardware.

Recent findings suggest that after pruning, the model trained on 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling model. This step recovered the performance the model had before pruning by training the remaining experts to take over the work of the ones that were deleted.

Following pruning and healing, Inkling 2 Mini underwent SFT with a similar data mix to Inkling 2 Small. This was followed by an RL that totaled 2.2T tokens over 2,000 steps. The post-training phase included on-policy distillation for training alignment, same as Inkling 2 Small.

Recent findings suggest that A key tool for understanding and overseeing an AI system is monitoring its chain of thought (CoT), the reasoning a model writes out as it works through a problem. The usefulness of CoT monitoring stems in part from the standard non-looped transformer architecture, in which each token passes through a fixed stack of layers once. This limits the number of sequential steps of computation the model can perform before it must output a token, so reasoning that needs more steps has to be carried out in generated text, where it can be read.

Looping a transformer’s layers raises this limit. By running the same layers multiple times, looped models increase their serial depth without adding more parameters, meaning that they do more computation per token internally before verbalizing their thought processes via CoT. Reasoning that never appears in the CoT can’t be caught by a CoT monitor, which has led to concerns that looped transformers could be harder to oversee.

In a recent development, one reason we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini is to enable the community to conduct research on looped transformers. We are particularly excited for researchers to investigate questions of monitorability, and to develop interpretability techniques for understanding the computation within loops.

In a recent development, to explore how different amounts of looping affect model properties like monitorability, we also trained a variable-looped model, TML-d24-varloop-research, because Inkling 2 Mini only supports a fixed number of looping passes. To enable variable looping, TML-d24-varloop-research was trained with between one and five looping passes.TML-d24-varloop-research was primarily trained for 3 passes of looping, with lower exposure to 1, 2, 4, and 5 passes. Performance at these latter pass counts may understate what training specifically for them could achieve. See the model card for details. We have also made this model publicly available on Hugging Face.

Below we describe our preliminary analysis of how looping affects monitorability. Overall, we find that looping increases what these models can do without a verbalized chain of thought, but at this scale we do not see a meaningful reduction in the monitorability of their reasoning.

Recent findings suggest that as a first step, we measured how much additional reasoning looping enables by comparing looped and non-looped models of the same size on tasks answered with no CoT at all. We used Think Fast, a benchmark that estimates a model’s no-CoT time horizon: the length of task, measured in human completion time, that a model can complete at 50% reliability without using CoT.These models were not trained to answer questions without a CoT. To elicit no-CoT answers, we prefilled the start of the response so that the model must answer directly, skipping reasoning. Other elicitation techniques, such as fine-tuning, might yield higher no-CoT performance and are worth exploring.

Sources indicate that as expected, looping increases no-CoT capability, though these gains eventually level off. The no-CoT time horizon of TML-d24-varloop-research rises from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds at three. Some of this is presumably due to the additional serial computation that looping provides. Beyond three passes, the time horizon is roughly flat. Interestingly, the model was never trained with more than five passes, and yet running it with ten does not significantly degrade its performance.

No-CoT 50% time horizon (human seconds).

As the number of looped passes increases past three, the gains are smaller, and on most tasks we observe similar performance. One exception is the N-Hop Lookup task, which cleanly evaluates serial reasoning: the model is given several lookup tables with fictional entries, and must follow a chain of lookups without writing anything down. We find that the model follows longer chains with more passes, improving out to ten loops.

In standard evaluations with CoT, we observe that more loop passes primarily benefit multi-hop reasoning rather than recall. Gains are largest on long-context retrieval (MRCR), followed by math and science reasoning (HMMT, GPQA Diamond, HLE) and long-horizon agentic tasks (SWE-bench Pro, BrowseComp). Closed-book factual QA is nearly invariant to loop passes (SimpleQA Verified, WorldVQA). See model card for full evaluations.

We next measured whether a model’s CoT reveals less about its reasoning as looping increases via two evaluations. First, we assessed how looping impacts the compression and legibility of a model’s CoT. Second, we measured how controllable a model’s CoT is, i.e., whether it can deliberately reshape its CoT to satisfy constraints. For each, we run TML-d24-varloop-research with one to five looped passes to study the effect of looping.

Note that TML-d24-varloop-research was only trained on variable pass counts from 1 to 5 during midtraining, and its RL was done with 3 passes. These experiments therefore do not tell us what a model trained with RL at a higher pass count would learn, and such a model might compress its reasoning more aggressively. A cleaner comparison would include every pass count in RL, which we leave to future work.

Industry observers note that compression and legibility. Since looping allows a model to spend more compute per token, we expect that it should need fewer CoT tokens to reach the same performance. We ran the variable-looped model at 1 to 5 passes, and found that as looping increases, the model generally achieves higher accuracy at each reasoning token budget, with diminishing returns after 3 passes. Notably, token efficiency on GPQA Diamond improves slightly from 3 to 5 passes, even though the model was trained with RL only at 3 passes, suggesting that some compression comes from additional computation itself, without RL at that depth.

Accuracy versus reasoning tokens.

DeepSWE v1.1 Accuracy (% of tasks resolved).

The observed CoT compression raises a question for monitorability: is shorter reasoning still readable, or does it omit notable details about the model’s thinking? We compared traces from the variable-looped model on the GPQA Diamond questions that it answered correctly at all five pass counts. Reasoning at 5 passes was less than half as long as at 1 pass (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens on average), but no less legible: sentence length and the fraction of words in an English dictionary were unchanged. On initial analysis, the difference is that the model is more direct and backtracks less on the way to the answer. The example below illustrates this difference on a simple question.

It has been revealed that march 1 falls on a Tuesday in a year that is not a leap year. What day of the week is May 20 of the same year? Give the final answer on its own last line as ANSWER: .

Controllability. One way that a model could evade monitoring is by steering its CoT away from anything a monitor would flag. The CoT-Control-QA evaluationReasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought, Yueh-Han et al., 2026 measures this capability by asking questions from GPQA, HLE and MMLU-Pro paired with an instruction about the CoT itself, such as avoiding a keyword from the question. Longer CoTs are generally harder to control, so we pool responses from five reasoning efforts (0.1, 0.2, 0.7, 0.9 and 0.99) and show controllability at matched CoT length.

Both Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research have poor control over their CoT. Among CoTs of 750–1,250 tokens, Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research (at 3 passes) follow the instruction at most 0.1% of the time, compared with 0.3% for Inkling 2 Small, 0.4% for Inkling-Small, and 1.3% for Qwen3.8-27B. Because the controllability rate is so low, this evaluation is unable to distinguish controllability between different amounts of looping.

Chain-of-thought controllability.

CoT controllability (log scale).

Sources indicate that to measure monitorability in agentic settings, we used LinuxArena, a control evaluation that measures whether an attacker model can perform malicious side tasks without detection when asked to perform a realistic software engineering task. We evaluated a helpful-only fine-tune of Inkling 2 Mini, since the released model refuses many of the side tasks. In absolute terms, both this model and TML-d24-varloop-research can be easily monitored by models like Qwen3.8-27B, which detected almost all side task attempts in our evaluation. To obtain relative rankings in monitorability, we tested a weaker model, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, as the monitor.

It has been revealed that with the monitor able to access only tool calls and outputs, it misses a significant number of the attacks. However, we see no clear trend with the number of looped passes.

Agentic monitorability will be key to track in larger-scale models, especially with architectures that allow for greater unverbalized thinking, and we encourage continued study of the impact of looping in this setting.

In a recent development, the goal of monitorability is to understand what a model is doing, and our main approach is to read its verbalized reasoning. Studying its internal computation directly, the aim of mechanistic interpretability, is another. Because looped transformers do more of their computation internally, we think they are a particularly interesting and notable setting for interpretability research, and we hope our looped models will be useful artifacts for the community.

We are working with the National Deep Inference Fabric (NDIF) to make these models more easily accessible to interpretability researchers. We also provided Goodfire, an interpretability research lab, early access to our looped models. They are working toward a mechanistic understanding of looped models, and have written up their early findings here.

According to recent reports, efficient intelligence makes Inkling 2 Mini a great choice for inference where speed is paramount, or for running on local hardware. At launch we support Inkling 2 Mini running on any Mac system (MacBook, Mac Mini) with at least 32GB RAM via Ollama. With native NVFP4 training and inference precision, Inkling 2 Mini runs efficiently on NVIDIA’s DGX Spark desktop AI computer. Quantized GGUF versions are available via Unsloth and llama.cpp for local inference.

In a recent development, inkling 2 Mini is available for inference and fine-tuning on Tinker, and for chat on the Tinker Playground. Open source inference is available on SGLang, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, NVIDIA Dynamo, TokenSpeed, and Llama App, with RL fine-tuning support on SkyRL, Miles, and NVIDIA AutoModel. Uber Is Testing Rides for Kids With Qualified Drivers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (446 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids.
  • The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
  • In a recent development, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The newly introduced program expands on the organization’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which debuted in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole upcoming influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

In a recent development, on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

First off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

It has been revealed that as any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

Sources indicate that according to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

It has been revealed that live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

In a recent development, uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release.
  • According to recent reports, but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04?
  • Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

According to recent reports, but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is at the moment expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

In a recent development, desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

In a recent development, one thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:.

With the repository added, you can install it with:.

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It has been revealed that it’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Also: Linux has hundreds of distros: 5 reasons to stop using the same few.

It’s been a very long time since Canonical had a disappointing release, and 27.04 will keep up that trend.
